    tsdst.distributions.dwrap¶

    tsdst.distributions.dwrap(data, params, disttype, funct, log=False, *, log_p=False)[source]¶

    Evaluate a distribution with separate log input and output options.

    This wrapper began as a way to evaluate common density and probability formulas through an R-like interface. Direct formulas were useful for performance comparisons in the original implementation. It now uses SciPy distributions for consistent parameter, support, and logarithmic-tail behavior.

    Parameters:
    dataarray-like

    Observation values for densities and probabilities. For quantiles, supply probabilities, or log probabilities when log_p=True. Values follow NumPy broadcasting rules with the parameter rows.

    paramsarray-like

    Supply one parameter set or a matrix with one set per row:

    • normal: (mu, sigma), where sigma is the standard deviation.

    • exponential: (rate,).

    • weibull: (shape, scale).

    • lnorm: (mu, sigma), the mean and standard deviation of log(X).

    • gamma: (shape, scale).

    Append the lower cutoff for either left-truncated operation. Shapes, scales, rates, and standard deviations must be positive. Invalid distribution parameters produce NaN.

    disttypestr

    All five distributions support these operations:

    • pdf: probability density.

    • cdf: cumulative probability.

    • sf: survival probability, P(X > data).

    • inv-cdf: quantile at the supplied probability.

    • left-truncated-cdf: cumulative probability conditional on X > cutoff.

    • left-truncated-inv-cdf: quantile conditional on X > cutoff.

    A truncated CDF is zero at and below the cutoff. If the cutoff is below the original support, the original lower bound still applies.

    functstr

    Choose normal, exponential, weibull, lnorm, or gamma.

    logbool, optional

    Return the natural logarithm of the output. This applies to every operation, including quantiles. A logged quantile is finite only when the quantile is positive. The default is False.

    log_pbool, optional

    Interpret quantile inputs as natural logarithms of probabilities. This follows R’s qnorm(..., log.p=TRUE) convention. Inputs must be at most zero. This option applies only to the two inverse-CDF operations. It does not change the output scale. The default is False.

    Returns:
    numpy.ndarray

    Density, probability, or quantile values on the requested output scale.

    Raises:
    ValueError

    If the distribution or operation is unknown, the number of parameters is wrong, or log_p is used for an operation other than a quantile.

    Notes

    For pdf, cdf, and sf, log=True follows R’s log-output convention. For quantiles, R uses log.p for the input scale. This wrapper uses log_p for that purpose and keeps log as the output switch. Both switches can be used together.

    Left truncation conditions on survival past the supplied cutoff. It can answer a future failure-probability question given survival to that time. A right-censored observation itself contributes a survival probability at its censoring time; that is distinct from a conditional truncated CDF.

    Sum log densities to obtain the log likelihood for independent observations. Negate that sum to obtain the negative log likelihood. Quantiles have a different role and do not return likelihoods.

    Examples

    >>> import numpy as np
>>> from tsdst.distributions import dwrap
>>> p = np.array([0.5, 0.975])
>>> dwrap(p, [0, 1], "inv-cdf", "normal")
array([0.        , 1.95996398])
>>> dwrap(np.log(p), [0, 1], "inv-cdf", "normal", log_p=True)
array([0.        , 1.95996398])
>>> dwrap([0.975], [0, 1], "inv-cdf", "normal", log=True)
array([0.6729261])
>>> dwrap([0, 1], [0, 1], "pdf", "normal", log=True)
array([-0.91893853, -1.41893853])
